name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+13, a steep structural advantage for Democrats
Incumbent Ed Case has a large financial edge, with $1.3M raised and $526K on hand against no reported challenger fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds around 96%
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, leaving the outlook dependent on fundamentals
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+13 electorate, a well-funded incumbent seeking reelection, a challenger with no reported fundraising, and market pricing near 96% for Democrats. With no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly twenty-plus points stands.
model.watch: Any emergence of challenger fundraising, outside spending, or polling showing unusual ticket-splitting in this low-profile race would be the first sign the margin could compress.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's first district, centered on urban Honolulu, leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Ed Case is running for another term with the usual advantages of office. He has raised about $1.3 million and holds more than $500,000 on hand, while Republican Adriel Lam reports no fundraising activity. A Green candidate and an independent are also on the ballot without visible resources.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings track this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing, which puts Democratic odds near 96%. The combination of a D+13 electorate, incumbency, and a decisive money edge makes an upset highly unlikely. The main caveat is that low-attention races can produce unpredictable turnout, but the structural margin here is wide enough to absorb ordinary noise.
